model.label: Single-payer National Health Insurance run by a government agency, funded mainly by income-related premiums paid by the insured, employers and the government

sources.title: National Health Insurance Annual Report 2025-2026 (bilingual)
sources.publisher: National Health Insurance Administration, Ministry of Health and Welfare, Taiwan
sources.funding_note: The insurer's own annual report (published November 2025); most figures refer to 2024. It presents the NHI favourably and cites commercial 'Health Care Index' rankings, which this profile does not use.

sources.title: National Health Expenditure 2024
sources.publisher: Department of Statistics, Ministry of Health and Welfare, Taiwan
sources.funding_note: Official national health accounts compiled to the OECD/Eurostat/WHO System of Health Accounts definitions; published February 2026, data for 2024. The summary text is in Chinese; tables are bilingual.

sources.title: 2024 Taiwan Health and Welfare Report
sources.publisher: Ministry of Health and Welfare, Taiwan
sources.funding_note: The ministry's own annual report; most figures refer to 2023.

sources.title: International Health Care System Profiles: Taiwan
sources.funding_note: Written by FT Longitude (Financial Times Group) for the Commonwealth Fund; data as of January 2026. Some figures rest on secondary or web sources and two out-of-pocket shares in the profile disagree (21.4% and 38.8%); neither is used here.

sources.title: Private Health Insurance in Taiwan: Insights From the US Medicare Program
sources.funding_note: A commentary, not original research. Dr Liao serves on the US Medicare Payment Advisory Commission (views his own).

sources.title: Advancing health technology assessment in Taiwan: over 15 years of evidence-based reform, innovation, and patient partnership
sources.publisher: International Journal of Technology Assessment in Health Care
sources.authors: Huang LY, Lin SY, Liu MH
sources.funding_note: A commentary written by staff of the Center for Drug Evaluation, the body that carries out the HTA it describes.

sources.title: Challenges and Contributing Factors to Emergency Department Overcrowding in Taiwan After the Lunar New Year Holiday: A 2024 Survey
sources.authors: Tai TL, Chou SF, Hsieh CC, Sim SS, Hung TY, Yeh YC, Tsai KC
sources.funding_note: Survey of ED directors at 59 hospitals one week after the February 2024 holiday; claims rest on the abstract.

sources.title: Preventable hospitalizations through ED: does the number of hospital beds matter under the global budget in a single-payer system in Taiwan?
sources.authors: Chen HF, Hsieh HM, Chang WS
sources.funding_note: Analysis uses 2011-2015 claims; only the paper's description of the current payment mechanism is used here.

sources.title: Health-related inequalities in out-of-pocket expenditure under universal health coverage in Taiwan: A cross-sectional decomposition analysis
sources.publisher: Journal of Health Services Research & Policy
sources.funding_note: National household survey of 657 people, January-August 2022. Claims rest on the PubMed abstract only.

sources.title: The Role of Digital Health Under Taiwan's National Health Insurance System: Progress and Challenges
sources.funding_note: Claims rest on the PubMed abstract only.
